title: How Anne Carson won her Nobel
gist: Jeremy Noel-Tod argues the Nobel in Literature has disproportionately gone to poets who write in prose forms, because prose-like, rhyme-free poetry translates across borders, and Anne Carson's hybrid verse-essay work fits this pattern.

insights.claim: An anthology of the prose poem found 13 Nobel laureates among its contents, suggesting the Nobel favours poets who stray into prose forms.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Noel-Tod
entities: Penguin Book of the Prose Poem
insights.so_what: A pattern in prize selection that helps predict future laureates: hybrid prose-poets.
insights.locator: Yet there in the table of contents were 13 Nobel laureates.

insights.claim: Poets who purge rhyme and metre in favour of looser prose modes produce work that translates more easily internationally, which helps explain Nobel preference for them.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Noel-Tod
insights.so_what: Translatability is an implicit selection factor for a global prize.
insights.locator: The wisdom of prose appeals to a world of prose.

insights.claim: The Cold War popularity of Eastern European poets in the West, including Polish laureates Milosz and Szymborska, was aided by the storyteller's ability to cross literary borders.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Noel-Tod
insights.locator: The storyteller's ability to cross literary borders

insights.claim: Carson's rise from university Classics instructor to Nobel laureate tracks the rise of Creative Writing in the academy and its relaxation of boundaries between humanities disciplines.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Noel-Tod
insights.so_what: Academic institutionalisation of hybrid forms is feeding mainstream recognition.
insights.locator: It's no coincidence that Carson's rise

insights.claim: Carson became the first woman to win the TS Eliot Prize, with The Beauty of the Husband (2001), and the first winner to combine poetry and scholarship.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Noel-Tod
insights.so_what: Marks her hybrid approach as an established prize-winning formula.

insights.claim: Her latest collection, Wrong Norma (2024), is mainly prose pieces, and the author finds it better for that, saying her line breaks can feel too heavy.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Noel-Tod
insights.so_what: Signals the author's view that her strongest work is in prose.
